He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[Houston Rockets]], [[Sacramento Kings]], [[New York Knicks]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Aldrich played three seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] before being drafted by the [[New Orleans Hornets]] with the 11th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. == Early life == Aldrich was born on October 31, 1988, in [[Burnsville, Minnesota]].{{cite web |title=Cole Aldrich Isn't Wasting Time Giving Back |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/community/cole-aldrich-isnt-wasting-time-giving-back |website=NBA |access-date=December 13, 2023 |date=September 7, 2016}} His father was a steel metal worker and his mother worked in an embroidery.{{cite web |title=Aldrich Brings Toughness, Dedication to Defensive End |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/aldrich_100709.html |website=NBA |access-date=December 13, 2023 |date=July 9, 2010}} Aldrich attended [[Bloomington Jefferson High School]] in [[Bloomington, Minnesota]].{{cite web |last1=Krawczynski |first1=Jon |title=Cole Aldrich, former Jayhawk: 'I've been a Timberwolves fan my whole life' |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/2016/07/14/cole-aldrich-former-jayhawk-ive-been-timberwolves-fan-my-whole-life/16581021007/ |website=The Topeka Capital-Journal |access-date=December 13, 2023 |date=July 14, 2016}} As a senior, he was named state player of the year by the [[St. Paul Pioneer Press]] and [[Minneapolis Star-Tribune]].{{cite web|title=Online Home of Cole Aldrich|url=http://www.colealdrich.com/|access-date=February 1, 2011|archive-date=February 8, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110208062237/http://colealdrich.com/|url-status=dead}} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Aldrich was listed as the No. 6 center and the No. 30 player in the nation in 2007.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Cole-Aldrich-24966;_ylt=AkdSkuEICIyzsxxrxw5uz.hGPZB4 Cole Aldrich Recruiting Profile] Retrieved January 28, 2015. ==College career== ===Freshman season=== [[File:Cole Aldrich cropped.jpg|thumb|Cole Aldrich against Iowa State on January 24, 2009]] During the 2007–08 season at [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], Aldrich's freshman season, his playing time was limited due to playing behind future [[NBA draft]] picks [[Darrell Arthur]], [[Sasha Kaun]], and [[Darnell Jackson]]. He averaged three rebounds and 2.8 points a game in 8.3 minutes a game during the regular season. Statistically, Aldrich's best performance was an 11-point, 11-rebound outing in a win over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]] on March 3, 2008.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=36170&year=2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604113809/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=36170&year=2008|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|title=Cole Aldrich Kansas Jayhawks Game Log (2007–08)|publisher=[[ESPN]]|year=2008|access-date=February 24, 2009}} Probably the most crucial game for Aldrich was during the Final Four game between Kansas and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] on April 5, 2008, when he played only 16 minutes but managed to grab 8 rebounds and score 7 points along with blocking 4 shots while also playing effective defense against National Player of the Year [[Tyler Hansbrough]], helping lead Kansas into the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA national championship game]]. They then defeated the [[Memphis Tigers]] to win their first Championship since 1988.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=284000031|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080408134344/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=284000031|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 8, 2008|title=North Carolina battles back, but Rush, Kansas close out Tar Heels|publisher=ESPN|date=April 6, 2008|access-date=February 24, 2009}} ===Sophomore season=== With the departure of the other Jayhawk big men to the NBA draft, Aldrich became the premier big man going into his sophomore season. Through the first 29 games, he averaged a double-double with 15.1 points and 10.8 rebounds in 29.7 minutes of play. He grabbed a career-high 20 rebounds in an 87–78 win over [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] on February 23, 2009.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290540201|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090228015105/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290540201|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 28, 2009|title=Taylor, Collins score 26 each as Jayhawks hand Sooners second straight loss|publisher=ESPN|date=February 24, 2009|access-date=February 24, 2009}} On March 8, 2009, Aldrich was named to the 2008–09 Big 12 All-conference first team.{{cite web|last=Bedore|first=Gary|title=Jayhawks well-represented on coaches' Big 12 teams|work=Lawrence Journal-World|publisher=The World Company|date=March 8, 2009|url=https://www2.kusports.com/news/2009/mar/08/jayhawks-well-represented-coaches-big-12-teams/|access-date=March 9, 2009}} On March 22, 2009, Aldrich recorded the first official [[triple-double]] in the history of Kansas basketball against Dayton in the second round of the NCAA tournament. Aldrich accumulated 13 points, 20 rebounds, and 10 blocks in a 60–43 victory, which was the second triple-double in NCAA history to include blocks, former [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] center [[Shaquille O'Neal]] recorded the other.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=294000056|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090325091004/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=294000056|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 25, 2009|title=Aldrich's 13 points, 20 boards, 10 blocked shots lead KU to Sweet 16|agency=Associated Press|work=ESPN|date=March 22, 2009|access-date=March 23, 2009}} On Monday, April 13, Aldrich announced that he would return to KU for his junior season. ===Junior season=== He won the 2009–10 men's college basketball [[Academic All-American]] of the Year as selected by [[CoSIDA]] and presented by ''[[ESPN the Magazine]]''.{{cite web |url=http://www.cosida.com/news/2010/2/22/0222105849_4996.aspx |title=Junior center Cole Aldrich of Kansas, Thomas More senior guard Daniel McKeehan lead ESPN the Magazine's Academic All-America Men's Basketball Teams |access-date=February 23, 2010 |date=February 22, 2010 |publisher=[[CoSIDA]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100226130801/http://cosida.com/news/2010/2/22/0222105849_4996.aspx |archive-date=February 26, 2010 |url-status=dead }} He ended his college career a perfect 55–0 at [[Allen Fieldhouse]]. ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2010–2012)=== On March 29, 2010, Aldrich announced that he would forgo his final season of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2010 NBA draft]]. He was the 11th pick, selected by the [[New Orleans Hornets]], who traded his rights on draft day to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. On August 6, 2010, Aldrich signed a two-year contract with the Thunder with a two-year option.{{cite web|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5442705&campaign=rss&source=twitter&ex_cid=Twitter_espn_5442705|title= Cole Aldrich signs with Thunder|date=August 6, 2010|access-date=August 6, 2010}} On November 24, 2010, the Thunder assigned Aldrich to the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the [[NBA D-League]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Assign Aldrich To Tulsa 66ers |access-date=November 25, 2010 |url=http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70242/20101124/thunder_assign_aldrich_to_tulsa_66ers/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125214341/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70242/20101124/thunder_assign_aldrich_to_tulsa_66ers/ |archive-date=November 25, 2010 |url-status=dead }} He was recalled on December 6, 2010,{{cite web|url=http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70447/20101206/thunder_recall_aldrich_from_d_league/ |title=Thunder Recall Aldrich From D-League |access-date=December 7, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101219074508/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70447/20101206/thunder_recall_aldrich_from_d_league/ |archive-date=December 19, 2010 |url-status=dead }} but sent back to Tulsa on December 30, 2010.{{cite web|date=December 30, 2010 |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70854/20101230/thunder_assign_aldrich_to_d_league/ |title=Thunder Assign Aldrich To D-League |access-date=December 30, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110102214428/http://basketball.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70854/20101230/thunder_assign_aldrich_to_d_league |archive-date=January 2, 2011 |url-status=dead }} He was again recalled on February 2, 2011, and assigned for a third time on March 30, 2011.{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2011-03-30-3020320363_x.htm|work=USA Today|title=Most Popular E-mail Newsletter|date=March 30, 2011|access-date=March 31, 2011}} Aldrich reached the [[2012 NBA Finals]] with the Thunder, but the team lost to the [[Miami Heat]]. ===Houston Rockets (2012–2013)=== In October 2012, Aldrich, [[James Harden]], [[Daequan Cook]], and [[Lazar Hayward]] were traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for [[Kevin Martin (basketball, born 1983)|Kevin Martin]], [[Jeremy Lamb]], and draft picks.{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder-acquires-martin-lamb-and-multiple-draft-picks-rockets|title=Thunder Acquires Martin, Lamb and Multiple Draft Picks from Rockets|access-date=October 28, 2012}} ===Sacramento Kings (2013)=== On February 20, 2013, Aldrich was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] along with [[Toney Douglas]] and [[Patrick Patterson (basketball)|Patrick Patterson]] in exchange for [[Francisco García (basketball)|Francisco García]], [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]] and [[Tyler Honeycutt]].{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-complete-multiplayer-trade|title=Kings Complete Multiplayer Trade|website=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2013|access-date=February 21, 2013}} ===New York Knicks (2013–2015)=== On September 24, 2013, Aldrich signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14311 |title=New York Knicks sign center Cole Aldrich |access-date=September 25, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130925175410/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14311 |archive-date=September 25, 2013 |url-status=dead }} On January 29, 2014, he was assigned to the Erie BayHawks.[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15145 Knicks assign Cole Aldrich, Toure Murry, Jeremy Tyler to D-League] Retrieved January 29, 2014. He was recalled the next day. He went on to record his first double-double (12 points, 10 rebounds) in his first NBA start on March 12, 2014.{{cite news|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/12/cole-aldrich-nearly-four-years-after-being-drafted-in-lottery-gets-double-double-in-first-career-start/|title=Cole Aldrich, nearly four years after being drafted in lottery, gets double-double in first career start|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=March 12, 2014|access-date=March 14, 2014}} On July 11, 2014, Aldrich re-signed with the Knicks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-re-sign-cole-adrich|title=Knicks Re-Sign Cole Adrich|website=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 11, 2014|access-date=July 12, 2014}} On April 11, 2015, he scored a career-high 19 points in an 80–79 win over the Orlando Magic.{{cite web|website=NBA.com|date=April 11, 2015|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20150411/NYKORL/gameinfo.html|title=Knicks hold off Magic, teams set NBA scoring low for quarter}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2015–2016)=== On July 13, 2015, Aldrich signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-austin-rivers-and-cole-aldrich|title=Clippers Sign Austin Rivers and Cole Aldrich|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2015|access-date=July 13, 2015}} On January 13, 2016, with starting center [[DeAndre Jordan]] out, Aldrich had a then season-best game with 19 points and 7 rebounds in a 104–90 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160113/MIALAC/gameinfo.html|title=Clippers win 10th straight, beat Heat 104–90 without Jordan|work=NBA.com|date=January 13, 2016|access-date=January 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331014450/http://www.nba.com/games/20160113/MIALAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 31, 2016|url-status=dead}} On April 8, 2016, he recorded 21 points and 18 rebounds (both season highs) and a career-high five steals in a 102–99 overtime win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/LACUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Crawford scores 30, including winner to lead Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2016|access-date=April 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160408065943/http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/LACUTA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 8, 2016|url-status=dead}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2016–2018)=== On July 13, 2016, Aldrich signed a three-year, $22 million deal with his hometown team, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-center-cole-aldrich|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN CENTER COLE ALDRICH|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2016|access-date=July 13, 2016}}{{cite 3, 2016|access-date=March 16, 2017}} On June 30, 2018, Aldrich was waived by the Timberwolves.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23955509/minnesota-timberwolves-waive-c-cole-aldrich|title=Timberwolves waive center Cole Aldrich|work=ESPN.com|date=June 30, 2018|access-date=June 30, 2018}} On September 18, 2018, Aldrich signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]]{{cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Cole Aldrich |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-sign-cole-aldrich |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 18, 2018 |date=September 18, 2018}} but was waived by the Hawks on October 2, 2018, as their first training camp cut.{{cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers on Cole Aldrich |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-cole-aldrich |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 2, 2018 |language=en |date=2018}} ===Tianjin Golden Lions (2018)=== On October 10, 2018, Aldrich signed with the [[Tianjin Golden Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web |title=Cole Aldrich officially signs with Tianjin Gold Lions |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cole-aldrich-officially-signs-with-tianjin-gold-lions/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 10, 2018 |archive-date=October 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191020101708/https://sportando.basketball/en/cole-aldrich-officially-signs-with-tianjin-gold-lions/ |url-status=dead }} He sprained his knee while playing and returned home.{{cite web |last1=Cacciola |first1=Scott |title=This Is What Life After the N.B.A. Looks Like |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/10/03/sports/basketball/nba-retirement.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=December 13, 2023 |date=October 3, 2022}} Aldrich planned to have a year-long break from basketball but made the decision to retire after his son was born and
